website_review.out_of_date_signs: Footer reads '© Robert M. Adochio, 2005'; no responsive design - the 390px view is a shrunken desktop page with ~8px text; no h1 and no page title beyond the attorney's name; no tel: link on the home page; static .html site with 14 links

No structured data, no service landing pages and no page title naming the service or town
Hours 'by appointment' only; the only intake path is a phone call or a Gmail address

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt allows all agents (User-agent: * with only Crawl-Delay: 20). Answerable: the services, three addresses and 'hours by appointment' are plain text, but there is no schema of any kind, no page title or h1 naming services, and no fee information. Bookable: the contact page offers only a phone number and adochiolaw@gmail.com - no form, no calendar, nothing an agent can complete. Findable: no rating surfaced in search beyond a small directory sample.

operations_signals.signal: Intake relies on a Gmail address and a phone line that the site says gets reviewed then answered manually
Three offices run on 'hours by appointment', which puts scheduling load on staff (inference)
The attorney also serves as municipal prosecutor and teaches, limiting hours available for intake and follow-up (inference from site content)

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add LocalBusiness/Attorney JSON-LD plus service+town pages so the practice is findable and quotable by AI answers

top_opportunities.opportunity: Simple AI intake/voicemail triage that captures matter type and books an appointment, given the by-appointment office model
top_opportunities.evidence: All scheduling is by phone/email with three offices on appointment-only hours

scores.reasons: The most outdated site in the batch - no mobile layout, no form, no schema, 2005 copyright - so almost everything is missing; small firm with modest budget though certified-trial PI work carries decent case values; a one-person consultancy could deliver a rebuilt site quickly; evidence is direct from the rendered page and its HTML.

businesses.name: Hoagland, Longo, Moran, Dunst & Doukas, LLP
businesses.what_they_do: Full-service defense-oriented law firm headquartered at 40 Paterson Street in New Brunswick, with 17 practice areas split between business practices and personal practices (defense litigation, insurance, employment, construction, professional liability, family/estate work). It advertises 40+ years in business, four offices and a client portal for institutional clients.
businesses.customers: Businesses, insurers, self-insureds and professionals needing defense counsel, plus some individual clients for personal legal matters.

size_signals.signal: '40+ YEARS IN BUSINESS', '4 NORTHEAST OFFICES', '17 PRACTICE AREAS'
Offices in New Brunswick NJ, Red Bank NJ, Hammonton NJ and 48 Wall Street, New York
Client portal, payment portal, careers page and a cases-and-verdicts section - indicates a sizable staff and formal back office

website_review.primary_cta: Menu-level 'CONTACT' and 'CALL US' items plus an 'Inquiries' form on the Offices page; client and payment portals
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: inquiry form only (Full Name, Email, Phone, Message) with a honeypot field; no appointment booking, which is normal for defense work
website_review.trust_signals: 40+ years, four offices, 17 practice areas, cases-and-verdicts directory, publications/blog, client portal
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Home page tagline ('looks after you, when you need us most') says nothing about what the firm does; no hours; no LocalBusiness/Attorney schema (Organization only); the office map images are generic grey placeholders (clear-practice-thumb.gif)
website_review.search_basics: Title covers New Jersey and New York law firm but not practice areas; practice-area and attorney directories exist with individual pages; JSON-LD is limited to a WebPage/Organization graph, no legal-specific schema
top_issues: Home page never states what the firm does or who it serves above the fold
No LocalBusiness/Attorney schema, no hours for any of the four offices, and placeholder map images
New-business intake is a single generic message form with no routing by practice group

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt not checked (data gap). Answerable: offices, phone numbers and 17 practice areas are plain text, but the site carries only a generic Organization schema - no LegalService/LocalBusiness, no hours and no attorney count, so answers about the firm are thin. Bookable: the inquiry form uses labelled fields and a honeypot rather than a CAPTCHA, so an AI agent could submit it; there is no calendar, which is reasonable for defense-firm new-business inquiries.

operations_signals.signal: Four offices, 17 practice areas and a formal client portal mean new-matter intake and conflicts screening are real administrative loads (inference)
Insights/blog, publications, events and cases-and-verdicts content require ongoing drafting and publishing work
Careers page exists, indicating ongoing hiring and HR administration

top_opportunities.opportunity: Structured new-matter intake for corporate/insurer inquiries that routes by practice group and captures conflicts data before a partner call
top_opportunities.evidence: Contact page exposes one generic message form with no practice-area routing across 17 practice areas

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add LegalService/Attorney schema, office hours and practice-area statements so AI answers and directory listings are accurate
top_opportunities.evidence: Only generic Organization JSON-LD; no hours anywhere; home page states no services above the fold

top_opportunities.opportunity: AI drafting assistant for the insights/publications pipeline (summaries, matter alerts) to feed the content engine
top_opportunities.evidence: Insights, news, events, publications, cases and blog sections all need continuous content

scores.reasons: A polished site that mainly needs schema, clearer positioning and intake routing rather than repair; a four-office, 17-practice defense firm clearly has budget; enterprise buying process, marketing/IT gatekeepers and conflict rules make delivery slow; evidence is decent on the website, weaker on internal operations.

caveats: Law firms were triaged as legal-service businesses; 'price ranges' are rarely published in this sector, contingency and free-consultation models are the closest equivalent and were checked where stated.

Two sites (ebm-law.com, stronglawoffice.com) returned 403 Unauthorized to the headless browser, so their phone-width rendering and robots.txt are unverified; assessments there come from fetched HTML and readable text.
Listing ratings for most firms were read from Birdeye/legal-directory aggregations of Google reviews rather than Google itself, and review counts vary between snapshots.
data_gaps: robots.txt not captured for rothenbergesq.com, familylawattorneyjersey.com and hoaglandlongo.com.
